(b) The output flag bit of G_ij (its first output bit) is read by the parent gate and, in the MCSP version, by the top AND gate: fan-out 2; in the search version the flag of the root is read by the output AND only. proved_step: LEMMA (repaired gate count for the MMW19 Lemma 3.1 tree; replaces S0003(c), see G0004). Let n >= 1, d >= 2, N_0 = 2^n, N_i = ceil(N_{i-1}/d) for i >= 1, D = least index with N_D = 1, G = sum_{i=1..D} N_i. Then (a) N_i = ceil(2^n / d^i) and D = ceil(log_d 2^n); (b) (d-1)*G <= 2^n - 1 + d*D. PROOF. (a) iterated ceiling division ceil(ceil(x/a)/b) = ceil(x/(ab)) for positive integers. (b) For integer x >= 0, ceil(x/d) <= x/d + 1, so N_i <= N_{i-1}/d + 1. Summing over i = 1..D: G <= (1/d) sum_{i=0}^{D-1} N_i + D. Telescoping: sum_{i=0}^{D-1} N_i = N_0 + (G - N_D) = 2^n + G - 1. Hence dG <= 2^n + G - 1 + dD, i.e. (d-1)G <= 2^n - 1 + dD. QED. Evidence: finite check cm-b51193b18e4e4a8b (n <= 20, 2 <= d <= 40: 0 violations, min slack 2), supporting only. CORRECTION (R1552, turn 18) to G0005: 'max reads per input bit' is not the right obstacle by itself. Layers compose multiplicatively: if each gate's replacement reads each of its input bits at most r times, leaf counts multiply by about r per layer, so after D = log_d(2^n) layers the leaf count is about r^D = N^(log_d r) with N = 2^n. So c = log_d r < 1 iff r < d, with d = l(n)/(100 s(n) log s(n)). HEURISTIC, NOT PROVED: the accounting ignores the l-fold input fan-in of each gate and the description-bit encoding; both must be included before the threshold r < d is trusted. S0005 (gate count) is unaffected and does not bound this. No P vs NP progress is claimed. lemma: LEMMA (tree-level reuse, source-checked; PROOF BY READING THE CONSTRUCTION of MMW19 Lemma 3.1, exact text fetched 2026-11-21). In the d-ary Circuit-Min-Merge tree, layer i+1 is the partition of layer i into consecutive blocks of d circuits, one gate per block. Hence every description D_{i,j} (i < top) is an input of exactly one gate G_{i+1,j'}, and every bottom description D_{0,j} is an input of exactly one gate G_{1,j'}. Consequence: between gates, the reuse r of a description is 1, so the leaf-exponent heuristic c = log r / log d with r = s (cm-4ca5cfd4ee5a4c25) is REFUTED as a description of the MMW tree. The inter-gate DAG is a tree; its unfolding has no blow-up from sharing. The only remaining reuse is INSIDE one Circuit-Min-Merge replacement, where the Sigma3SAT^A formula checks the d input circuits on their intervals and may read each input bit more than once.

proved_step: LEMMA U (unfolding bound, conditional on depth; statement exact). Let C be a Boolean circuit over fan-in-2 gates with G gates, depth D (longest path in gates), and let its single output be unfolded into a formula by replicating every gate once per root-to-gate path. Then the formula has at most 2^(D+1) - 1 nodes. Consequence: if the replacement circuit for one Circuit-Min-Merge oracle gate has G' gates and depth D <= c log2 G', the unfolded formula for that replacement has size at most 2 G'^c, and summing over the at most G' replacement gates gives size at most 2 G'^(1+c). Proof: a tree of depth D with branching at most 2 has at most sum_{i=0}^{D} 2^i = 2^(D+1) - 1 nodes; the depth hypothesis gives 2^(D+1) <= 2 G'^c; the sum over gates is at most G' times the per-gate bound. Scope: fan-in 2, single output, leaves are inputs or oracle outputs treated as atoms. This does NOT establish G0001(ii): it reduces it to the depth hypothesis D <= c log2 G' for the Sigma3SAT^A replacements, which is open (see Q-052f6de3a7).
